title: introduce-binary-delta-upgrades-for-cutlass-triton-and-safe-rollback-paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Upgrading CUTLASS/Triton/CUDA kernels currently requires shipping full kernel bundles which increases upgrade blast radius, prolongs maintenance windows, and complicates canaries. We still see transient startup failures in mixed-fleet clusters when large binary swaps occur.

Goal: Implement a binary-delta upgrade path and safe rollback controls for kernel bundles so that: 1) most upgrades transmit and apply smaller deltas instead of full bundles, 2) canary nodes can validate deltas independently before broader rollout, and 3) live rollback is fast and reliable. This reduces network egress, deployment time, and probe-related flakiness during upgrades.

Scope: design and implement a delta-generator for kernel bundles, extend the runtime's kernel loader to support applying signed deltas atomically, add verification hooks and staged canary semantics, and expand CI to validate delta generation across supported CUDA/CUTLASS/Triton version pairs. Integrate with existing artifact signing and release metadata so rollbacks and rollforwards are auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Delta generator produces deterministic binary deltas between two kernel-bundle versions for all supported bundle shapes (full static libs, .so collections, and quantized artifacts)
Runtime loader can apply a delta atomically and fall back to full bundle if delta application fails; failures are logged with diagnostic bundle and checksum
Signed deltas are verified by the runtime using existing release signing keys; signature verification failure prevents apply
Canary workflow implemented: zone-based canary (1%) + progressive rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on health regression
CI job (ci/kernel-delta-check) validates delta generation and applies it against a miniature canary cluster in preprod for at least 3 версия pairs
Documentation and runbook updated with steps to inspect delta application, force-fallback, and manual rollback
No increase in 95th percentile startup latency in canary clusters after delta rollout (goal: +/-5% of baseline)
Production rollout performed behind feature flag and monitored by existing runtime SLO dashboards (tokenized traces + kernel-load errors)
work_notes: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting — agreed on delta format (bsdiff-like patch for ELF/so + manifest mapping for kv-cache layout). Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Priya (Build), Jens (Runtime) — action: prototype delta generator (Priya) and loader hooks (Jens)

2026-03-04: Prototype delta generator (repo: github.com/redwood-inference/kernel-delta) created. Initial implementation targets single .so bundles; observed non-determinism due to build timestamps — added deterministic build wrapper in ci/build/kernel-det.sh

2026-03-06: PoC loader integrated into runtime branch feature/delta-loader. Loader supports dry-run apply and checksum compare. Observed an edge case where PTX embedded metadata offsets shift; added manifest-relative offsets to delta spec

2026-03-09: Security reviewed signing approach with SRE. Decided to reuse release keys and extend signature envelope to include source bundle checksum and base-version field. Security TODO: formal FIPS-compatible signing path in Private deployments

2026-03-12: Integration test added to ci/kernel-delta-check that generates a delta between v1.18-cutlassA and v1.19-cutlassB, then applies to a k8s micro-canary cluster (cluster: canary-delta-us-west2). Observed one failure where delta applied but a symbol version mismatch occurred on CUDA 12.1 nodes; mitigation: loader will trigger full-bundle fallback and capture coredump for analysis

2026-03-14: Begin canary rollout in preprod using feature flag runtime.delta_apply.enabled=true for 2 pods in canary pool. Monitoring dashboards: monitoring.redwood/runtime/kernel-delta. No regressions detected in first 6 hours
testing_plan: Unit tests for delta-generator (binary equivalence after apply) in kernel-delta repo
Fuzz test: random chunk reordering and corrupted delta detection paths
Hardware matrix runs: CUDA 11.7 / 11.8 / 12.0 / 12.1 on NVIDIA A10/A30/A100 variants in CI-lab
Preprod canary: apply delta to 1% of nodes, hold for 2h with synthetic load that exercises KV cache warmup and long-context generation
Rollback test: intentionally induce apply failure and verify runtime falls back to full bundle and marks the delta as bad in artifact store
End-to-end perf test: measure cold-start and 95th percentile latency against baseline on canary nodes
Security test: signature validation failure modes (expired key, tampered delta) and Private deployment sign/verify validation
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Feature off in prod, rollout to preprod canaries only (completed)
Phase 1 - Canary 1% of production nodes in region us-west2 for 24h with health checks and automated rollback on >0.5% kernel-load-errors
Phase 2 - Progressive rollout to 10% then 50% with 4h observation windows
Phase 3 - Full rollout with post-rollout validation (72h health window) and audit of delta artifacts
Rollback: immediate rollback flips runtime.delta_apply.enabled=false or forces runtime.delta_apply.mode=fallback, and postmortem of failed delta
risks: Delta application could succeed but leave subtle ABI incompatibilities that only surface under long request sequences
Non-deterministic deltas caused by build-time metadata could create mismatched apply results across nodes
Compromised signing keys would allow malicious deltas unless we enforce additional runtime allowlists in Private deployments
Increased complexity in runtime loader could add new failure modes and make debugging harder for on-call engineers
mitigations: Add deterministic-build wrapper and CI gate to refuse non-deterministic bundles
Run extended load tests on canaries for 48h before wide rollout to catch long-tail failures
Introduce a delta-reputation store: deltas with repeated fails are blacklisted automatically
Keep full-bundle fallback fast and well-instrumented with auto-collected diagnostics (stack traces, loader logs, artifact checksums)
Require sign-off from Runtime and SRE leads before Phase 2 rollout
